paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: The perplexity standard deviations when only PvCs are reserved at each layer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the standard deviation of perplexity (log-scaled) across different layers of a model when only the PvC (Projection Value Cache) components are retained at each layer. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," ranges from 0 to 35 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 10. The y-axis, labeled "Perplexity (log) Std," ranges from 0.00 to 1.75 with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 0.25. A single orange line with diamond-shaped markers connects data points across the layers. At Layer 0, the perplexity standard deviation is approximately 1.75, which then sharply drops to around 0.30 at Layer 1. From Layer 1 to Layer 35, the values continue to decline gradually, reaching approximately 0.05 by Layer 35, and remain nearly flat for the remainder of the layers. The plot includes a grid with dashed lines for both axes to aid in reading the values.
